AccountRename.description: Rename the account, set its type (one with no API), or both; type_key null clears it.
AccountRename.title: AccountRename

BinanceDifferenceOut.description: A reconciliation difference that still holds: where and when, never an amount.
BinanceDifferenceOut.title: BinanceDifferenceOut

CardMerchantRegister.description: The own accounts card payments to a Monzo merchant go into; none removes it.
CardMerchantRegister.title: CardMerchantRegister

CardMerchantSuggestionOut.description:
A card merchant whose website is on a connected platform's domain, offering the
platform's accounts; registering it is register_card_merchant.
CardMerchantSuggestionOut.title: CardMerchantSuggestionOut

CashFlowHiddenAccountOut.description: Money moved between an account left out of reports and those still in them.
CashFlowHiddenAccountOut.title: CashFlowHiddenAccountOut

CashFlowOut.description: Income and spending in the reporting currency; spending is positive.
CashFlowOut.title: CashFlowOut

CsvColumns.description: Column names in the file; several description columns are joined with one space.
CsvColumns.title: CsvColumns

CsvExtract.description:
Typed fields read out of one column: the first pattern that matches a non-empty cell
in full fills the fields its named groups name (those that match); a cell no pattern
matches makes the row an error.
CsvExtract.title: CsvExtract

FamilyNotes.description:
Whether a row moved money within its account's family, as `column` says (account
family identifier design §5.9): for a row whose type (the type column's value) is one
of `types`, a stripped cell matching one of `within` in full is a move within the
family (family_move true), one matching one of `outside` a movement outside it (false),
and any other a row error naming the column and the rule, never the value. Every other
row's family_move is None: the profile says nothing of it.
FamilyNotes.title: FamilyNotes

IdentifierHoldersRegister.description:
The own accounts payments to an identifier go into: a card merchant (`value` its
Monzo merchant id, as CardMerchantRegister), or a UK bank account several own accounts
are paid through (`value` its sort code and account number, e.g. "11-22-33 12345678");
none removes them.
IdentifierHoldersRegister.title: IdentifierHoldersRegister

ImportStatementOut.description: What the file says at statement level; fields it doesn't print are null.
ImportStatementOut.title: ImportStatementOut

IncomeEntryOut.description: The positive flows of one transaction in one instrument, added up.
IncomeEntryOut.title: IncomeEntryOut

IncomeOut.description: What came in over a range, in the reporting currency.
IncomeOut.title: IncomeOut

PairCandidateOut.description: A record the owner could pair with another as one transfer.
PairCandidateOut.title: PairCandidateOut

ReviewOut.description:
A value two sources of one event disagree on (design §5.7): open, or resolved by the
owner taking one of them.
ReviewOut.title: ReviewOut

ReviewResolve.description: Which source's value the owner takes for a review item.
ReviewResolve.title: ReviewResolve

TransactionCategoriesUpdate.description: Set the owner's category on transactions, or clear it with null.
TransactionCategoriesUpdate.title: TransactionCategoriesUpdate

TransferOut.description:
A transfer as matching left it. Its id changes when matching reopens it, so a client
finds it again by its own records' ids.
TransferOut.title: TransferOut

get.description: Where Monzo sends the browser back: exchange the code, then wait for approval.

put.description:
Replace the key (a new one after the old was rejected). It must belong to the account
already connected. It is also how a disabled connection is brought back (adding the account
again is refused as a duplicate): the ledger, cursors and config are kept. Only a
connection disabled when the update began is brought back: a disable made while the key
was checked stands.

Replace the two keys. The sync's gate checks that they are read-only and belong to
the same user; a disabled connection is checked first, as a create is (the read-only
gate), and is healthy again.

post.description:
Ingest an eToro account statement (xlsx) the owner downloaded, normalise it with the
API's records and heal the transfers, in one command (design §5.3). Its file is written
last, just before the commit: a refused or failed upload leaves none behind.

put.description: Replace the token, its expiry and the query id (a new token after the old one expired).

post.description:
Ingest a Flex statement the owner downloaded: the closed ISA, which the Flex Web
Service can't fetch. It goes through the same ingest and normalise as a fetched one.

get.description:
The connection's review items (design §5.7): open ones first, newest first. Only an
eToro or a Trading 212 connection has them.

post.description:
Take one source's value, recorded as the owner's decision, and normalise at once so the
decision posts now, then heal the transfers the new postings touch.

put.description:
Replace the key and secret. The sync checks that they belong to the same account; a
disabled connection is checked first, as a create is, and is healthy again.

post.description:
Ingest a Trading 212 CSV export the owner downloaded, normalise it with the API's
records and heal the transfers, in one command. Optional: it adds what the API lacks.
Its file is written last, just before the commit: a refused or failed upload leaves none
behind.

get.description:
The account types the owner can pick: where an account's data comes from and how it
posts. Only a type with no API creates an account here; one with an API is connected.

post.description:
Register a Monzo card merchant as paying into these own accounts (a suggestion, too),
replacing the accounts it had; none removes the registration. Every record naming it is
matched again; Monzo's next sync names it on the payments made before.

Register the own accounts an identifier pays into, replacing the ones it had; none
removes them. A UK bank account several of your accounts are paid through (a platform's
client money account) must be registered to no account. Every record naming it is
matched again.

patch.description:
Rename the account, set its type, or both, in one command: if either is refused,
neither happens. Setting or clearing the type needs an account that can take imports (a
connector owns a connected account's); a type must have no API and agree with the
account's shape. type_key null clears it.

post.description: Switch a snapshots account to hybrid, so it can carry identifiers.
Close the account; it stays a holder of the card merchants it held.

Register one of the account's identifiers (a suggestion, too): every record naming
it is matched again.

delete.description:
Take the identifier off the account; the registry row stays, as transactions name
it, and the records naming it are matched again.

post.description: Give a manual account a main account, or clear it; its transfers are matched anew.
Leave the account out of net worth, holdings and cash flow, or put it back.

get.description:
Income and spending by period, category and payee, without the accounts left out of
reports; defaults to the 365 days up to and including today.

Holdings valued in the reporting currency, without the accounts left out of reports
unless `all_accounts`; the date defaults to today.
Each supported bank's export formats with a ready profile config (one recommended).

post.description: Upload a statement file and stage it for review; nothing is posted until commit.

get.description:
Daily net worth, without the accounts left out of reports; defaults to the 365 days up
to and including today.

put.description: Set the owner's category on the transactions, or clear it with null. All or nothing.

post.description:
The owner says two own records are one transfer, whether or not either is in one:
in one instrument of opposite, equal amounts, or two currencies of opposite sign that
differ in currency or in amount (the receiving side not larger). Undone by unpairing
the resulting transfer.

get.description:
The own records the record could be paired with as one transfer, on another account:
those of the opposite and equal amount first, then those in a currency whose side
differs (`differs`: in currency or in amount) booked within 7 days; each part nearest
booking date first, at most 20 in all.

post.description: Void the transaction; a transfer it was a side of follows (heal).

get.description:
Bank accounts and chain addresses that own records name and that are neither
registered nor dismissed, most named first (registering one is add_account_identifier);
then card merchants on a connected platform's domain (kind card_merchant; registering
one is register_card_merchant).

post.description: The owner says the card merchant pays into none of their accounts.
The owner says the bank account is not one of theirs.

get.description: Transfers, newest first; only those of the given statuses when any are given.

The own records that could be the transfer's missing side: those of the same amount
first, then those of another, then those the owner unpaired from it (which pair can
link again); empty for a transfer with both sides.

post.description:
The owner picks the transfer's missing side among its candidates, or one they
unpaired from it. Two currencies may differ in currency or in amount (settled by a
conversion, or the difference a fee); anything else must be of the same instrument and
amount.
The owner says it is not a transfer: its records go back to Unassigned.

The owner says the matched transfer's two records are not one transfer; each is
matched again, never with the other.
Withdraw a rejection; its records are matched again (under a new transfer id).
